extraction.body: It is an ambitious social experiment of our moment in history — one that experts say could accomplish something that parents, schools and other governments have attempted with varying degrees of success: keeping kids off social media until they turn 16. Australia's new law, approved by its Parliament last week, is an attempt to swim against many tides of modern life — formidable forces like technology, marketing, globalization and, of course, the iron will of a teenager. And like efforts of the past to protect kids from things that parents believe they're not ready for, the nation's move is both ambitious and not exactly simple, particularly in a world where young people are often shaped, defined and judged by the online company they keep. Stream NBC10 Boston news for free, 24/7, wherever you are. The ban won't go into effect for another year. But how will Australia be able to enforce it? That's not clear, nor will it be easy. TikTok, Snapchat and Instagram have become so ingrained in young people's lives that going cold turkey will be difficult. Other questions loom. Does the ban limit kids' free expression and — especially for those in vulnerable groups — isolate them and curtail their opportunity to connect with members of their community? And how will social sites verify people's ages, anyway? Can't kids just get around such technicalities, as they so often do? This is, after all, the 21st century — an era when social media is the primary communications tool for most of those born in the past 25 years who, in a fragmented world, seek the common cultures of trends, music and memes. What happens when big swaths of that fall away? Is Australia's initiative a good, long-time-coming development that will protect the vulnerable, or could it become a well-meaning experiment with unintended consequences? The law will make platforms including TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat, Reddit, X and Instagram liable for fines of up to 50 million Australian dollars ($33 million) for systemic failures to prevent children younger than 16 from holding accounts. “It’s clear that social media companies have to be held accountable, which is what Australia is trying to do,” said Jim Steyer, president and CEO of the nonprofit Common Sense Media. Leaders and parents in countries around the world are watching Australia’s policy closely as many seek to protect young kids from the internet's dangerous corners — and, not incidentally, from each other. Most nations have taken different routes, from parental consent requirements to minimum age limits. Many child safety experts, parents and even teens who have waited to get on social media consider Australia's move a positive step. They say there’s ample reason to ensure that children wait. “What’s most important for kids, just like adults, is real human connection. Less time alone on the screen means more time to connect, not less," said Julie Scelfo, the founder of Mothers Against Media Addiction, or MAMA, a grassroots group of parents aimed at combatting the harms of social media to children. “I’m confident we can support our kids in interacting in any number of ways aside from sharing the latest meme.” The harms to children from social media have been well documented in the two decades since Facebook’s launch ushered in a new era in how the world communicates. Kids who spend more time on social media, especially as tweens or young teenagers, are more likely to experience depression and anxiety, according to multiple studies — though it is not yet clear if there is a causal relationship. What's more, many are exposed to content that is not appropriate for their age, including pornography and violence, as well as social pressures about body image and makeup. They also face bullying, sexual harassment and unwanted advances from their peers as well as adult strangers. Because their brains are not fully developed, teenagers, especially younger ones the law is focused on, are also more affected by social comparisons than adults, so even happy posts from friends can send them into a negative spiral. Many major initiatives, particularly those aimed at social engineering, can produce side effects — often unintended. Could that happen here? What, if anything, do kids stand to lose by separating kids and the networks in which they participate? Paul Taske, associate director of litigation at the tech lobbying group NetChoice, says he considers the ban “one of the most extreme violations of free speech on the world stage today" even as he expressed relief that the First Amendment prevents such law in the United States "These restrictions would create a massive cultural shift,” Taske said. “Not only is the Australian government preventing young people from engaging with issues they’re passionate about, but they’re also doing so even if their parents are ok with them using digital services," he said. "Parents know their children and their needs the best, and they should be making these decisions for their families — not big government. That kind of forcible control over families inevitably will have downstream cultural impacts.” David Inserra, a fellow for Free Expression and Technology, Cato Institute, called the bill “about as useful as an ashtray on a motorbike” in a recent blog post. While Australia's law doesn't require “hard verification” such as an uploaded ID, he said, it calls for effective “age assurance.” He said no verification system can ensure accuracy while also protecting privacy and not impacting adults in the process. Privacy advocates have also raised concerns about the law's effect on online anonymity, a cornerstone of online communications — and something that can protect teens on social platforms. “Whether it be religious minorities and dissidents, LGBTQ youth, those in abusive situations, whistleblowers, or countless other speakers in tricky situations, anonymous speech is a critical tool to safely challenge authority and express controversial opinions,” Inserra said. A spot check of kids at one mall in the Australian city of Brisbane on Wednesday didn't turn up a great deal of worry, though. “Social media is still important because you get to talk to people, but I think it’s still good that they’re like limiting it,” said Swan Son, a 13-year-old student at Brisbane State High School. She said she has had limited exposure to social media and wouldn’t really miss it for a couple of years. Her parents already enforce a daily one-hour limit. And as for her friends? “I see them at school every day, so I think I’ll be fine.” Conor Negric, 16, said he felt he’d dodged a bullet because of his age. Still, he considers the law reasonable. “I think 16 is fine. Some kids, I know some kids like 10 who’re on Instagram, Snapchat. I only got Instagram when I was 14." His mom, Sive Negric, who has two teenage sons, said she was happy for her boys to avoid exposure to social media too early: “That aspect of the internet, it’s a bit `meanland.'" Parents in Britain and across Europe earlier this year organized on platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram to promise not to buy smartphones for children younger than 12 or 13. This approach costs almost no money and requires no government enforcement. In the United States, some parents are keeping kids off social media either informally or as part of an organized campaign such as Wait Until 8th, a group that helps parents delay kids' access to social media and phones. This fall, Norway announced plans to ban kids under 15 from using social media, while France is testing a smartphone ban for kids under 15 in a limited number of schools — a policy that could be rolled out nationwide if successful. U.S. lawmakers have held multiple congressional hearings — most recently in January — on child online safety. Still, the last federal law aimed at protecting children online was enacted in 1998, six years before Facebook’s founding. In July, the U.S. Senate overwhelmingly passed legislation designed to protect children from dangerous online content, pushing forward with what would be the first major effort by Congress in decades to hold tech companies more accountable. But the Kids Online Safety Act has since stalled in the House. While several states have passed laws requiring age verification, those are stuck in court. Utah became the first state to pass laws regulating children’s social media use in 2023. In September, a judge issued the preliminary injunction against the law, which would have required social media companies to verify the ages of users, apply privacy settings and limit some features. NetChoice has also obtained injunctions temporarily halting similar laws in several other states. And last May, U.S. Surgeon General Vivek Murthy said there is insufficient evidence to show social media is safe for kids. He urged policymakers to treat social media like car seats, baby formula, medication and other products children use. “Why should social media products be any different? Scelfo said. “Parents cannot possibly bear the entire responsibility of keeping children safe online, because the problems are baked into the design of the products.”

extraction.body: BOSTON — For parents who remember growing up with a house phone, going “old school” may be one of the newest technology trends for kids. Some local families are turning to Wi-Fi-enabled house phones as a way for children to call friends without giving them a smartphone or access to social media. For the Gay family in Medway, that means using a device called a Tin Can phone. “One of our neighbors found it, and kind of sent it all out to us and said we should get this for the neighborhood, and we were immediately on board,” said Medway mother Frances Gay. “This was the beginning of the summer. They’ve been using it all summer, and it’s really worked out well.” The phone works over Wi-Fi and allows children to call approved phone numbers. Parents can control which numbers are permitted to call the phone. For Frances and Ed Gay, the device gives their children some independence to communicate with friends without some of the concerns that come with smartphones. “When they first started using it, they’d just pick the phone up. We’d be like, ‘You have to speak,’” Ed Gay said. “I think it’s been great for them to learn communication skills.” The couple hopes alternatives like the house phone will allow them to delay giving their children smartphones and access to social media. “I think the longer we can wait, the better off we are,” Ed Gay said. Concerns grow over social media’s impact on kids The push by some parents to delay social media comes amid growing concern about the effect the platforms can have on children. Dr. James McKowen, a clinical psychologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, sees the negative impacts firsthand. “I work with a lot of parents who, when they try to set limits and boundaries on their phones, their kids get aggressive; they get angry,” McKowen said. “It’s like cutting off their arm in some ways. They just really can’t be separated from their phone.” McKowen said some young people find it difficult to stop using the platforms and that excessive use can interfere with their mood, sleep, time outdoors and socialization. “A decent proportion do find it very hard to stop,” he said. McKowen said social media can also affect developing brains, contributing to issues involving attention spans, impulse control, anxiety and depression. Federal lawmakers consider social media restrictions for children Lawmakers are also considering new restrictions aimed at children’s access to social media. U.S. Rep. Jake Auchincloss is co-sponsoring the “16 and Up Social Media Act,” along with “Parents Over Platforms,” which would establish a national standard prohibiting social media use for children under 16. “These children are functionally laborers in a system of dopamine extraction,” Auchincloss said. Under the proposal described by Auchincloss, parents would enter a child’s birthday into a smartphone. When an app is downloaded, the app would receive an anonymized signal indicating whether the user falls within the permitted age range. “Every time an app is downloaded into the app store, an anonymized age signal is sent up to that app, and all it says is this individual is or isn’t within the age bounds that your app is bound to,” Auchincloss said. McKowen said he believes social media restrictions for young people should be viewed similarly to age restrictions placed on other products. “Just like we think about cigarette use, alcohol use, cannabis use for young people, we’ve got limits on it, we’ve got age restrictions,” McKowen said. “Social media should really be thought of similarly.” State lawmakers in Massachusetts are also considering restrictions on social media. For families like the Gays, broader rules could make it easier for parents who are trying to delay their children’s introduction to social media. “I’d love for this to go into place before this becomes a problem for us,” Frances Gay said. passages: BOSTON — For parents who remember growing up with a house phone, going “old school” may be one of the newest technology trends for kids.
Some local families are turning to Wi-Fi-enabled house phones as a way for children to call friends without giving them a smartphone or access to social media.
For the Gay family in Medway, that means using a device called a Tin Can phone.

“One of our neighbors found it, and kind of sent it all out to us and said we should get this for the neighborhood, and we were immediately on board,” said Medway mother Frances Gay. “This was the beginning of the summer. They’ve been using it all summer, and it’s really worked out well.”
The phone works over Wi-Fi and allows children to call approved phone numbers. Parents can control which numbers are permitted to call the phone.
For Frances and Ed Gay, the device gives their children some independence to communicate with friends without some of the concerns that come with smartphones.
“When they first started using it, they’d just pick the phone up. We’d be like, ‘You have to speak,’” Ed Gay said. “I think it’s been great for them to learn communication skills.”
The couple hopes alternatives like the house phone will allow them to delay giving their children smartphones and access to social media.
“I think the longer we can wait, the better off we are,” Ed Gay said.
Concerns grow over social media’s impact on kids
The push by some parents to delay social media comes amid growing concern about the effect the platforms can have on children.
Dr. James McKowen, a clinical psychologist at Massachusetts General Hospital, sees the negative impacts firsthand.

“I work with a lot of parents who, when they try to set limits and boundaries on their phones, their kids get aggressive; they get angry,” McKowen said. “It’s like cutting off their arm in some ways. They just really can’t be separated from their phone.”
McKowen said some young people find it difficult to stop using the platforms and that excessive use can interfere with their mood, sleep, time outdoors and socialization.
“A decent proportion do find it very hard to stop,” he said.
McKowen said social media can also affect developing brains, contributing to issues involving attention spans, impulse control, anxiety and depression.
Federal lawmakers consider social media restrictions for children
Lawmakers are also considering new restrictions aimed at children’s access to social media.

U.S. Rep. Jake Auchincloss is co-sponsoring the “16 and Up Social Media Act,” along with “Parents Over Platforms,” which would establish a national standard prohibiting social media use for children under 16.
“These children are functionally laborers in a system of dopamine extraction,” Auchincloss said.

Under the proposal described by Auchincloss, parents would enter a child’s birthday into a smartphone. When an app is downloaded, the app would receive an anonymized signal indicating whether the user falls within the permitted age range.

“Every time an app is downloaded into the app store, an anonymized age signal is sent up to that app, and all it says is this individual is or isn’t within the age bounds that your app is bound to,” Auchincloss said.
McKowen said he believes social media restrictions for young people should be viewed similarly to age restrictions placed on other products.

“Just like we think about cigarette use, alcohol use, cannabis use for young people, we’ve got limits on it, we’ve got age restrictions,” McKowen said. “Social media should really be thought of similarly.”
State lawmakers in Massachusetts are also considering restrictions on social media.
For families like the Gays, broader rules could make it easier for parents who are trying to delay their children’s introduction to social media.
“I’d love for this to go into place before this becomes a problem for us,” Frances Gay said.
Changes expected for young social media users

The changes come as Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, is expected to implement additional restrictions and safety features for minors following a multi-billion-dollar settlement this summer. The lawsuit claimed the social media company made its apps addicting to children on purpose.

The 2024 PGA Tour season is winding down towards its conclusion, but before we reach the RSM Classic there are still two more events to play - starting with this week's $7.2 million World Wide Technology Championship . Each of the golfers in the FedEx Cup Fall tournament will be hoping to improve upon their positions in the standings, be it by either trying to jump into the top-70 on the season or simply securing their full-time playing rights for 2025. As we approach the last-chance saloon for a number of recognizable names on the PGA Tour, the pressure to achieve their respective goals will be rising with each passing round. Ahead of the 2024 World Wide Technology Championship, four of the Golf Monthly team have selected a handful of likely contenders... El Cardonal at Diamante is Tiger Woods' first design used by the PGA Tour El Cardonal at Diamante is located in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico and represents Tiger Woods' first design used by the PGA Tour. The 7,363-yard, par-72 layout opened in 2014 and is well known for its extremely forgiving fairways and mammoth-size greens. As a result, finding the fairway and putting surface is not as much of a challenge as usual. This was highlighted by Adam Long's feat of hitting every fairway for the week in 2023. With the area only receiving something like six inches of rain per year, the ground conditions in the desert area unsurprisingly play extremely firm and fast. This helps golf balls trickle into the rustic bunkers which are often placed in the middle of desired landing areas. And the range of elevation - around 240 feet - from the 17th tee to the third fairway makes El Cardonal a pretty taxing walk for players and caddies alike. Nevertheless, the resort course is extremely scoreable, reflected by van Rooyen's winning 27-under total last season, and is expected to produce another birdie-fest in 2024. Matti Schmid at the 2024 Shriners Children's Open I backed Schmid last time out in Vegas and he finished T3rd after posting a fifth-place result at the Black Desert Championship the week prior. The former Open silver medallist is yet to win as a pro but has two third-place finishes on the PGA Tour. He is gaining experience quickly and is a brilliant putter so should be able to make plenty of birdies in Mexico this week on what is a very low-scoring course. The scoring will be low at the WWT Championship and Tom Hoge leads the PGA Tour in birdies made courtesy of his superb iron play (fourth on tour) and solid putting stats. It’s not necessarily a bomber’s paradise, looking at last year’s leaderboard, so the fairly short-hitting Hoge has the skills to challenge if he can get off to a quick start. Hall has played some of the best golf of his career of late, getting his first PGA Tour win at the ISCO Championship just a few months ago. He has recorded two top-15 finishes in his last two starts and shot 65 or better in his five of his last 15 PGA Tour rounds. The ability to go low is going to be important here, especially on a simple-enough resort style course, and Hall has certainly proven he can do that. The Englishman ranks third for Birdie Average on the PGA Tour this season, and has previously scored well at similar style courses (Vidanta - Mexico Open), so at this price he certainly ticks a lot of boxes. Kizzire is another player with a recent win and the ability to go low when necessary, so I can't really work out why his price is so huge. A missed cut last time out will have been disappointing, but he didn't play terribly and can be forgiven when you consider he was 11th at the Sanderson Farms Championship just three starts back. Kizzire has shot 66 or better in five of his last 17 rounds, ranks fifth for Birdie Average on the PGA Tour, and finished T10th at this event last year after posting back-to-back 65s to start the week. At this price, he is a very interesting contender in the each-way betting market. He's in good form and, with a week's break to rest and recover, I fancy Ghim to finally get over the line at a course where he finished in a share of 15th last year. What's more, if you looked at his form during that period, he had missed two cuts coming into the World Wide Technology Championship whereas, this time around, he's playing a lot better. Arriving at a course that you know you can play well, will be a big confidence booster. I backed Bridgeman at the Sanderson Farms Championship and he finished in a share of 11th. Since then, he has registered a modest tie for 46th and 29th. Why I have gone for him again this week is purely down to his stats in relation to approach play and on the greens. Last year, Adam Long hit every fairway off the tee, so the wide layout isn't going to be much trouble for the world's best. Also, the greens at El Cardonal are enormous, so it'll be the approach play and on the greens that will likely decide the winner of this tournament. Looking at the stats, Bridgeman ranks well in this area, which is why I have opted for him again. The winner this week will need to be an explosive and prolific scorer, and Schmid fits the bill perfectly. He is a long and accurate driver (not necessarily that important this week, granted), he has definitely found something with his approach play as he gained strokes on the field in that category in four of the past five weeks, and it's a similar story in terms of his putting - arguably the strongest part of Schmid's game right now. Coming off the back of two top-fives and a T16th before that, I have a good feeling that Schmid may pick up his first PGA Tour success if it all comes together. Ahead of the 2024 World Wide Technology Championship, four of the Golf Monthly team have selected a handful of likely contenders...
El Cardonal at Diamante is Tiger Woods' first design used by the PGA Tour
El Cardonal at Diamante is located in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico and represents Tiger Woods' first design used by the PGA Tour.

The 7,363-yard, par-72 layout opened in 2014 and is well known for its extremely forgiving fairways and mammoth-size greens. As a result, finding the fairway and putting surface is not as much of a challenge as usual. This was highlighted by Adam Long's feat of hitting every fairway for the week in 2023.

With the area only receiving something like six inches of rain per year, the ground conditions in the desert area unsurprisingly play extremely firm and fast. This helps golf balls trickle into the rustic bunkers which are often placed in the middle of desired landing areas.

And the range of elevation - around 240 feet - from the 17th tee to the third fairway makes El Cardonal a pretty taxing walk for players and caddies alike. Nevertheless, the resort course is extremely scoreable, reflected by van Rooyen's winning 27-under total last season, and is expected to produce another birdie-fest in 2024.
Matti Schmid at the 2024 Shriners Children's Open
I backed Schmid last time out in Vegas and he finished T3rd after posting a fifth-place result at the Black Desert Championship the week prior.

The former Open silver medallist is yet to win as a pro but has two third-place finishes on the PGA Tour. He is gaining experience quickly and is a brilliant putter so should be able to make plenty of birdies in Mexico this week on what is a very low-scoring course.
The scoring will be low at the WWT Championship and Tom Hoge leads the PGA Tour in birdies made courtesy of his superb iron play (fourth on tour) and solid putting stats.
It’s not necessarily a bomber’s paradise, looking at last year’s leaderboard, so the fairly short-hitting Hoge has the skills to challenge if he can get off to a quick start.

Hall has played some of the best golf of his career of late, getting his first PGA Tour win at the ISCO Championship just a few months ago. He has recorded two top-15 finishes in his last two starts and shot 65 or better in his five of his last 15 PGA Tour rounds.

The ability to go low is going to be important here, especially on a simple-enough resort style course, and Hall has certainly proven he can do that. The Englishman ranks third for Birdie Average on the PGA Tour this season, and has previously scored well at similar style courses (Vidanta - Mexico Open), so at this price he certainly ticks a lot of boxes.

Kizzire is another player with a recent win and the ability to go low when necessary, so I can't really work out why his price is so huge. A missed cut last time out will have been disappointing, but he didn't play terribly and can be forgiven when you consider he was 11th at the Sanderson Farms Championship just three starts back.

Kizzire has shot 66 or better in five of his last 17 rounds, ranks fifth for Birdie Average on the PGA Tour, and finished T10th at this event last year after posting back-to-back 65s to start the week. At this price, he is a very interesting contender in the each-way betting market.
He's in good form and, with a week's break to rest and recover, I fancy Ghim to finally get over the line at a course where he finished in a share of 15th last year.

What's more, if you looked at his form during that period, he had missed two cuts coming into the World Wide Technology Championship whereas, this time around, he's playing a lot better. Arriving at a course that you know you can play well, will be a big confidence booster.
I backed Bridgeman at the Sanderson Farms Championship and he finished in a share of 11th. Since then, he has registered a modest tie for 46th and 29th.

Why I have gone for him again this week is purely down to his stats in relation to approach play and on the greens. Last year, Adam Long hit every fairway off the tee, so the wide layout isn't going to be much trouble for the world's best.

Also, the greens at El Cardonal are enormous, so it'll be the approach play and on the greens that will likely decide the winner of this tournament. Looking at the stats, Bridgeman ranks well in this area, which is why I have opted for him again.

The winner this week will need to be an explosive and prolific scorer, and Schmid fits the bill perfectly. He is a long and accurate driver (not necessarily that important this week, granted), he has definitely found something with his approach play as he gained strokes on the field in that category in four of the past five weeks, and it's a similar story in terms of his putting - arguably the strongest part of Schmid's game right now.
Coming off the back of two top-fives and a T16th before that, I have a good feeling that Schmid may pick up his first PGA Tour success if it all comes together.

extraction.body: The PGA Tour is staying in Mexico this week and heading south to Cabo San Lucas, where El Cardonal at Diamante awaits a competitive field led by 2025 champion Ben Griffin and the reigning Haskins Award winner Jackson Koivun . While Griffin and Koivun might be considered the headliners for the World Wide Technology Championship, oddsmakers have tapped Ryan Gerard as the pre-tournament favorite. Gerard, who has eight finishes inside the top 10 this season , comes into Mexico after shooting four consecutive sub-70 rounds at the Baycurrent Classic in Japan. Here’s a look at where Griffin, Koivun and the rest of the field slot in after Gerard on the odds board. 2026 World Wide Technology Championship odds (courtesy of DraftKings, as of November 2) World Wide Technology Championship winner prediction The top of the board presents some intriguing options, especially with Gerard coming in fully rested and primed to notch his second career victory on Tour. But we’re feeling a bit burned from our Wyndham Clark recommendation last week so going a bit deeper and suggesting Kris Ventura at +3900. Ventura was exceptional over the weekend in Vallarta, playing his final 27 holes bogey-free on his way to a T-2 finish . We see no reason why his driver should cool off in Cabo. He currently ranks fifth in shots gained off the tee and third in total driving. And with a hot boom stick, Ventura has seen his approach game start to thrive — he sits 10th in greens in regulation percentage and 19th in proximity to the hole. David Ford isn’t too far down the listed favorites at +5200, and we expect the UNC alum to play motivated against his fellow Tar Heels (Gerard and Griffin). Before being cut last week, Ford had finished T-3 in Utah and T-25 at the abbreviated tournament in Bermuda, so we like his late-season form. Additionally, the 24-year-old Ford should be properly motivated sitting No. 125 in the FedExCup Fall standings. Two more while we’re here: Beau Hossler (+6000) and Austin Hitt (+8000) Who will lead after Round 1 in Cabo San Lucas? Nothing about his last 12 rounds screams ‘Take me!’ but we’re going with a gut feel here and offer Jackson Suber at +4600. The 2024 PGA Tour season is winding down towards its conclusion, but before we reach the RSM Classic there are still two more events to play - starting with this week's $7.2 million World Wide Technology Championship . Each of the golfers in the FedEx Cup Fall tournament will be hoping to improve upon their positions in the standings, be it by either trying to jump into the top-70 on the season or simply securing their full-time playing rights for 2025. As we approach the last-chance saloon for a number of recognizable names on the PGA Tour, the pressure to achieve their respective goals will be rising with each passing round. Ahead of the 2024 World Wide Technology Championship, four of the Golf Monthly team have selected a handful of likely contenders... El Cardonal at Diamante is Tiger Woods' first design used by the PGA Tour El Cardonal at Diamante is located in Cabo San Lucas, Mexico and represents Tiger Woods' first design used by the PGA Tour. The 7,363-yard, par-72 layout opened in 2014 and is well known for its extremely forgiving fairways and mammoth-size greens. As a result, finding the fairway and putting surface is not as much of a challenge as usual. This was highlighted by Adam Long's feat of hitting every fairway for the week in 2023. With the area only receiving something like six inches of rain per year, the ground conditions in the desert area unsurprisingly play extremely firm and fast. This helps golf balls trickle into the rustic bunkers which are often placed in the middle of desired landing areas. And the range of elevation - around 240 feet - from the 17th tee to the third fairway makes El Cardonal a pretty taxing walk for players and caddies alike. Nevertheless, the resort course is extremely scoreable, reflected by van Rooyen's winning 27-under total last season, and is expected to produce another birdie-fest in 2024. Matti Schmid at the 2024 Shriners Children's Open I backed Schmid last time out in Vegas and he finished T3rd after posting a fifth-place result at the Black Desert Championship the week prior. The former Open silver medallist is yet to win as a pro but has two third-place finishes on the PGA Tour. He is gaining experience quickly and is a brilliant putter so should be able to make plenty of birdies in Mexico this week on what is a very low-scoring course. The scoring will be low at the WWT Championship and Tom Hoge leads the PGA Tour in birdies made courtesy of his superb iron play (fourth on tour) and solid putting stats. It’s not necessarily a bomber’s paradise, looking at last year’s leaderboard, so the fairly short-hitting Hoge has the skills to challenge if he can get off to a quick start. Hall has played some of the best golf of his career of late, getting his first PGA Tour win at the ISCO Championship just a few months ago. He has recorded two top-15 finishes in his last two starts and shot 65 or better in his five of his last 15 PGA Tour rounds. The ability to go low is going to be important here, especially on a simple-enough resort style course, and Hall has certainly proven he can do that. The Englishman ranks third for Birdie Average on the PGA Tour this season, and has previously scored well at similar style courses (Vidanta - Mexico Open), so at this price he certainly ticks a lot of boxes. Kizzire is another player with a recent win and the ability to go low when necessary, so I can't really work out why his price is so huge. A missed cut last time out will have been disappointing, but he didn't play terribly and can be forgiven when you consider he was 11th at the Sanderson Farms Championship just three starts back. Kizzire has shot 66 or better in five of his last 17 rounds, ranks fifth for Birdie Average on the PGA Tour, and finished T10th at this event last year after posting back-to-back 65s to start the week. At this price, he is a very interesting contender in the each-way betting market. He's in good form and, with a week's break to rest and recover, I fancy Ghim to finally get over the line at a course where he finished in a share of 15th last year. What's more, if you looked at his form during that period, he had missed two cuts coming into the World Wide Technology Championship whereas, this time around, he's playing a lot better. Arriving at a course that you know you can play well, will be a big confidence booster. I backed Bridgeman at the Sanderson Farms Championship and he finished in a share of 11th. Since then, he has registered a modest tie for 46th and 29th. Why I have gone for him again this week is purely down to his stats in relation to approach play and on the greens. Last year, Adam Long hit every fairway off the tee, so the wide layout isn't going to be much trouble for the world's best. Also, the greens at El Cardonal are enormous, so it'll be the approach play and on the greens that will likely decide the winner of this tournament. Looking at the stats, Bridgeman ranks well in this area, which is why I have opted for him again. The winner this week will need to be an explosive and prolific scorer, and Schmid fits the bill perfectly. He is a long and accurate driver (not necessarily that important this week, granted), he has definitely found something with his approach play as he gained strokes on the field in that category in four of the past five weeks, and it's a similar story in terms of his putting - arguably the strongest part of Schmid's game right now. Coming off the back of two top-fives and a T16th before that, I have a good feeling that Schmid may pick up his first PGA Tour success if it all comes together. extraction.body: The PGA Tour is staying in Mexico this week and heading south to Cabo San Lucas, where El Cardonal at Diamante awaits a competitive field led by 2025 champion Ben Griffin and the reigning Haskins Award winner Jackson Koivun . While Griffin and Koivun might be considered the headliners for the World Wide Technology Championship, oddsmakers have tapped Ryan Gerard as the pre-tournament favorite. Gerard, who has eight finishes inside the top 10 this season , comes into Mexico after shooting four consecutive sub-70 rounds at the Baycurrent Classic in Japan. Here’s a look at where Griffin, Koivun and the rest of the field slot in after Gerard on the odds board. 2026 World Wide Technology Championship odds (courtesy of DraftKings, as of November 2) World Wide Technology Championship winner prediction The top of the board presents some intriguing options, especially with Gerard coming in fully rested and primed to notch his second career victory on Tour. But we’re feeling a bit burned from our Wyndham Clark recommendation last week so going a bit deeper and suggesting Kris Ventura at +3900. Ventura was exceptional over the weekend in Vallarta, playing his final 27 holes bogey-free on his way to a T-2 finish . We see no reason why his driver should cool off in Cabo. He currently ranks fifth in shots gained off the tee and third in total driving. And with a hot boom stick, Ventura has seen his approach game start to thrive — he sits 10th in greens in regulation percentage and 19th in proximity to the hole. David Ford isn’t too far down the listed favorites at +5200, and we expect the UNC alum to play motivated against his fellow Tar Heels (Gerard and Griffin). Before being cut last week, Ford had finished T-3 in Utah and T-25 at the abbreviated tournament in Bermuda, so we like his late-season form. Additionally, the 24-year-old Ford should be properly motivated sitting No. 125 in the FedExCup Fall standings. Two more while we’re here: Beau Hossler (+6000) and Austin Hitt (+8000) Who will lead after Round 1 in Cabo San Lucas? Nothing about his last 12 rounds screams ‘Take me!’ but we’re going with a gut feel here and offer Jackson Suber at +4600. sources.title: New York Times and other outlets sue web browser Brave over alleged content scraping
passages: The New York Times sued Brave, the 11-year-old, privacy-focused browser company, on Monday, alleging it scraped the outlet’s copyrighted content and unlawfully distributed it to customers the suit names as Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere.
“In this way, Brave acts both like a burglar that misappropriates the content of publishers, and an AI ‘fence’ that sells stolen content to third parties,” the suit reads.
It says Brave built an index of more than 30 billion web pages using an unidentified crawler, leaving publishers unable to block it.
Founded in 2015, Brave has raised roughly $250 million to date, according to private-market trackers.
The suit also targets a Brave browser feature that bypasses paywalls and the company’s practice of blocking publishers’ ads while selling its own.
Brave did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Separately on Monday, the Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel filed a similar lawsuit. Both were brought in federal court in Manhattan. The New York Times, which has also sued OpenAI and Perplexity over similar claims, likens Brave to a “supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content” for AI companies. “In this way, Brave acts both like a burglar that misappropriates the content of publishers, and an AI ‘fence’ that sells stolen content to third parties,” the suit reads. It says Brave built an index of more than 30 billion web pages using an unidentified crawler, leaving publishers unable to block it. The suit also targets a Brave browser feature that bypasses paywalls and the company’s practice of blocking publishers’ ads while selling its own. Founded in 2015, Brave has raised roughly $250 million to date, according to private-market trackers. The Times seeks an injunction and damages. Brave did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

sources.title: Who's suing AI and who's signing latest: US newspapers sue Brave Software and Canadian publishers sue Anthropic - Press Gazette
passages: A group of US newspapers including The New York Times have sued Brave Software, a group of Canadian news publishers are suing Anthropic, and Reach and CNN are the latest news publishers to sign an AI deal with Google.
21 October 2026: Canadian publishers Postmedia, Torstar, The Globe and Mail and The Canadian Press have filed a copyright lawsuit against Anthropic.
They are the first publishers being tracked by Press Gazette to sue Anthropic, following behind only Reddit.

Steven Lieberman, attorney for the MediaNews Group and Tribune Publishing plaintiffs, said: “AI giants are now desperate to avoid getting caught red-handed stealing news from publishers, so Brave Software is selling them a back door to the journalism they know they have no right to.
Buying stolen goods secondhand doesn’t make them legitimate.
Brave must be held responsible for laundering pirated reporting for the AI industry.”

In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs allege that “Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere”.

The publishers said in a statement: “News media companies invest hundreds of millions of dollars into reporting Canadians’ critical stories, undertaking investigations and original reporting, and distributing media in both official languages in every province and territory across this country.
The publishers say Anthropic used their content to develop its AI model Claude.
— News Corp is suing the privacy-focused browser Brave, accusing it of scraping and selling its copyrighted content to AI companies.

“Companies like Brave incorporated copyrighted works into their products and services to generate revenue for themselves, all while destroying the incentive for anyone to ever pay the very publishers who produced the content that Brave has monetised,” the lawsuit said.

The publishers involved are: Advance Local Media, Conde Nast, The Atlantic, Forbes, The Guardian, Business Insider, LA Times, McClatchy Media Company, Newsday, Plain Dealer Publishing Company, Politico, The Republican Company, Toronto Star Newspapers, and Vox Media.
They claim Cohere copies publisher content even when it is behind a paywall or when a website has blocked its bot from scraping.

Reuters, which said it has seen the court filing, reported that the publishers argued OpenAI presented “a clear and present danger to the valuable copyrights” of DNPA members and other news titles through its “wilful scraping … and adaptation of content”.

Participants include New York State local newspaper owner Richner Communications, several subsidiaries of AIM Media Management, CherryRoad Media Inc, Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Rust Publishing, Sentinel Media Co, Shaw Family Holdings and Straus Newspapers Inc.

Other recent developments in terms of deals and litigation between publishers and AI firms include the following: — A judge has found it plausible that Perplexity conspired to bypass access controls and obtain Reddit’s material using third-party data scrapers, rejecting a motion to dismiss the case. — News Corp is suing the privacy-focused browser Brave, accusing it of scraping and selling its copyrighted content to AI companies. — Microsoft has signed its first deal for news content in the Asia Pacific region with Australia’s Nine Entertainment. If you feel there is something missing that should be included, or you want to alert us to a new development, please contact charlotte.tobitt@pressgazette.co.uk. 2 November 2026 : US newspapers The New York Times, The Chicago Tribune, The Orlando Sentinel and The Daily News have sued Brave Software, maker of Brave web browser, for stealing their news articles for use by AI giants such as Anthropic. The NYT was first to sue Brave, accusing the company of scraping its journalism and selling access to it to AI companies. It was reported that hours later the three other publishers alleged that Brave uses their copyrighted content to generate AI responses, sells access to stolen content to other AI companies, allows users to bypass publisher paywalls and blocks publisher adverts while substituting these with their own. Both cases were brought in federal court in Manhattan, and both focus on the same part of Brave’s business: its search index and the data it makes available to AI developers. Steven Lieberman, attorney for the MediaNews Group and Tribune Publishing plaintiffs, said: “AI giants are now desperate to avoid getting caught red-handed stealing news from publishers, so Brave Software is selling them a back door to the journalism they know they have no right to. Buying stolen goods secondhand doesn’t make them legitimate. Brave must be held responsible for laundering pirated reporting for the AI industry.” In the lawsuit, the plaintiffs allege that “Brave is the supplier, dealer, and distributor of stolen copyrighted content for its own users and many of the most prominent GenAI companies, including Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, and Cohere”. 21 October 2026: Canadian publishers Postmedia, Torstar, The Globe and Mail and The Canadian Press have filed a copyright lawsuit against Anthropic. The publishers say Anthropic used their content to develop its AI model Claude. They are the first publishers being tracked by Press Gazette to sue Anthropic, following behind only Reddit. 7 September 2026: The Seattle Times and Newsday, a local news publication covering Long Island and New York City, have filed a joint lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft. Similar to other cases filed against the tech companies, the publishers alleged that their content, including paywalled articles, has been obtained via scraping, whether by OpenAI and Microsoft or third parties, and used within large-scale datasets on which their generative AI products are trained and grounded, all without permission. Both The Seattle Times and Newsday previously received grant funding to hire an AI fellow from OpenAI and Microsoft via The Lenfest Institute for Journalism in 2024. The Wall Street Journal owner alleged that before March 2025, Brave scraped and sold copyrighted News Corp content to AI companies that were “in direct competition with the News Corp Companies’ own content licensing programmes”. “Companies like Brave incorporated copyrighted works into their products and services to generate revenue for themselves, all while destroying the incentive for anyone to ever pay the very publishers who produced the content that Brave has monetised,” the lawsuit said. It follows Brave filing its own lawsuit against News Corp in February in response to a cease-and-desist from the news publisher, arguing that Brave AI was indexing website content. Brave said this is what “all search engine operators must do to exist”. Participants include New York State local newspaper owner Richner Communications, several subsidiaries of AIM Media Management, CherryRoad Media Inc, Arkansas Democrat-Gazette, Rust Publishing, Sentinel Media Co, Shaw Family Holdings and Straus Newspapers Inc. 29 May 2026: CNN is suing Perplexity , launching its first lawsuit against an AI company to oppose the alleged stealing of its copyrighted content. It said it believed Perplexity had unlawfully copied more than 17,000 CNN stories, videos, images and other works to power its tools. 13 February 2025: A collection of news and magazine publishers who are members of the US News/Media Alliance have filed a copyright suit against Canadian AI start-up Cohere Inc. The publishers involved are: Advance Local Media, Conde Nast, The Atlantic, Forbes, The Guardian, Business Insider, LA Times, McClatchy Media Company, Newsday, Plain Dealer Publishing Company, Politico, The Republican Company, Toronto Star Newspapers, and Vox Media. extraction.body: Fondaction and Triodos Bank demonstrate at COP17 how innovative finance can accelerate the implementation of global biodiversity goals MONTREAL, Oct. 25, 2026 /CNW/ -- At COP17, Fondaction and Triodos Bank are sending a clear signal that natural capital is becoming an investable asset class. Value Nature Fund, developed jointly by Fondaction Asset Management and Triodos Investment Management, provides a concrete example: a natural capital investment strategy designed to unlock institutional capital for the restoration of farms, forests, and the ecosystems they depend on. For every dollar invested in protecting nature, US$30 is spent on activities that degrade it, according to UNEP's State of Finance for Nature 2026 report. Yet, restoring natural capital can strengthen the long-term resilience and productive capacity of farms and forests by improving the health of the ecosystems they depend on. Closing this gap requires moving beyond commitments and scaling nature-positive investment solutions. Value Nature Fund offers a concrete response by mobilising institutional capital toward the restoration of farms and forests while generating long-term value for investors, biodiversity, climate and communities. Value Nature Fund is targeting € 300 million (US$ 337 million) and intends to invest in farms and forests across Europe and North America, transitioning them toward regenerative and resilient practices. Sustainable agriculture and forestry investment opportunities remain fragmented, limiting institutional investors' ability to deploy capital at scale. Value Nature Fund seeks to address this gap by building a diversified natural capital investment strategy backed by real assets. The Fund brings together the complementary expertise of Fondaction Asset Management and Triodos Investment Management to demonstrate that investing in the restoration of natural capital can support biodiversity and climate objectives while creating long-term value for investors. "The challenge is no longer simply to recognize the value of nature. We need to create financial solutions that allow capital to actively contribute to its restoration. Together with Triodos, we are turning our shared conviction into action, bringing complementary expertise from both sides of the Atlantic to help make natural capital accessible at institutional scale." Stéphan Morency, President and Chief Executive Officer of Fondaction "The urgency of addressing biodiversity loss and climate change continues to grow. Value Nature Fund demonstrates the power of collaboration: combining our expertise with Fondaction's enables us to mobilise institutional capital to restore farms, forests and the ecosystems our economies depend on. Together, we aim to finance change and change finance by making natural capital investable at scale." Hadewych Kuiper, Managing Director Triodos Investment Management The approach behind Value Nature Fund aligns with the objectives of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework to better integrate biodiversity into financial decision-making and mobilise significantly more resources for nature. "Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity calls for mobilizing financial resources from all sources. As highlighted in the Global Report, significant gaps remain, including private finance. I hope Value Nature Fund will help demonstrate how clarity and confidence in potential financial returns can be achieved, addressing one of the key barriers to unlocking and scaling up investment in nature." Astrid Schomaker, Executive Secretary, Convention on Biological Diversity "Public resources remain essential, but they cannot meet the financing needs of biodiversity protection and restoration on their own. We need to expand the role of private investment, integrate nature-related risks and opportunities into financial decision-making, and develop credible mechanisms that support measurable and lasting outcomes. I congratulate Fondaction and Triodos for making Value Nature Fund a concrete example of alignment between finance and biodiversity action." Mr. Robert Abisoghomonyan, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Trade of the Republic of Armenia Value Nature Fund has received commitments from Fondaction and Triodos Bank to the amount of C$25 million and €5 million (US$ 5.6 million) respectively as founding investors in Value Nature Fund, conditional upon reaching a first close. The initiative builds on both organisations' experience in impact investing and reflects a shared ambition: to move beyond measuring nature-related risks and start mobilising capital at the scale needed to restore natural systems. Value Nature Fund is a natural capital investment strategy designed to invest in vital farms and forests and supports their transition toward regenerative and closer-to-nature practices. The fund seeks to generate financial returns while restoring ecosystems, strengthening biodiversity and building long-term resilience. The strategy brings together the complementary expertise of Canadian impact-driven asset manager Fondaction Asset Management and Dutch impact investor Triodos Investment Management . For more information, please visit valuenaturefund.com . Fondaction Asset Management (FAM) is an impact-driven manager that creates and delivers innovative, high-performance financial solutions to solve major environmental and social issues, generating competitive returns. As a subsidiary of Fondaction, a labor-sponsored fund from Montréal, Québec, Canada, FAM channels large-scale capital into high-potential impact sectors, accelerating the sustainable transformation of the economy. FAM currently manages fund platforms in areas such as energy transition, natural capital protection, environmental markets, and the circular economy. For more information, please visit fondactionassetmanagement.ca or follow us on LinkedIn . Triodos Investment Management is a pure-play impact investor with a global reach. We enable professional investors to leverage their capital to drive positive social and environmental change, offering a comprehensive range of impact investment solutions across all asset classes. Our investment strategy is centered around five key transitions: Food, Resources, Energy, Society and Wellbeing. These themes reflect our commitment to advancing the transition towards a green, resilient and inclusive economy. Triodos Investment Management is a wholly owned subsidiary of Triodos Bank, a leading expert in sustainable banking, with €6 billion in assets under management as of 30 June 2026. For more information, please visit triodos-im.com or follow us on LinkedIn . Disclaimer: This publication does not constitute an offer or invitation to subscribe for units in Value Nature Fund I. The information contained therein should not be relied upon as it is incomplete and subject to change. For purposes of the Triodos Investment Management managed vehicle of Value Nature Fund I, this document is a pre-marketing communication testing potential investor interest in the Dutch fund vehicle by Triodos Investment Management. To this end, this document, as far as it relates to the Dutch fund vehicle, is only intended for professional investors based in Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Spain and Sweden. This pre-marketing communication in relation to the Dutch vehicle of Value Nature Fund I is thus not intended for any other investors including professional investors based in countries other than the aforementioned.

I congratulate Fondaction and Triodos for making Value Nature Fund a concrete example of alignment between finance and biodiversity action." Mr. Robert Abisoghomonyan, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Trade of the Republic of Armenia

Value Nature Fund has received commitments from Fondaction and Triodos Bank to the amount of C$25 million and €5 million (US$ 5.6 million) respectively as founding investors in Value Nature Fund, conditional upon reaching a first close. The initiative builds on both organisations' experience in impact investing and reflects a shared ambition: to move beyond measuring nature-related risks and start mobilising capital at the scale needed to restore natural systems.

Value Nature Fund is a natural capital investment strategy designed to invest in vital farms and forests and supports their transition toward regenerative and closer-to-nature practices. The fund seeks to generate financial returns while restoring ecosystems, strengthening biodiversity and building long-term resilience.
The strategy brings together the complementary expertise of Canadian impact-driven asset manager Fondaction Asset Management and Dutch impact investor Triodos Investment Management .
For more information, please visit valuenaturefund.com .

Fondaction Asset Management (FAM) is an impact-driven manager that creates and delivers innovative, high-performance financial solutions to solve major environmental and social issues, generating competitive returns.

As a subsidiary of Fondaction, a labor-sponsored fund from Montréal, Québec, Canada, FAM channels large-scale capital into high-potential impact sectors, accelerating the sustainable transformation of the economy. FAM currently manages fund platforms in areas such as energy transition, natural capital protection, environmental markets, and the circular economy.
For more information, please visit fondactionassetmanagement.ca or follow us on LinkedIn .

Triodos Investment Management is a pure-play impact investor with a global reach. We enable professional investors to leverage their capital to drive positive social and environmental change, offering a comprehensive range of impact investment solutions across all asset classes.

Our investment strategy is centered around five key transitions: Food, Resources, Energy, Society and Wellbeing. These themes reflect our commitment to advancing the transition towards a green, resilient and inclusive economy. Triodos Investment Management is a wholly owned subsidiary of Triodos Bank, a leading expert in sustainable banking, with €6 billion in assets under management as of 30 June 2026.
For more information, please visit triodos-im.com or follow us on LinkedIn .

Since the signing of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework in 2022, the world has made strides in developing solutions that unlock finance for nature and climate. Two years on, the upcoming UN Conference of Parties for Biological Diversity (CBD COP16) provides an opportunity to take stock of these finance trends, and further raise ambition to close the finance gap to halt and reverse the decline of nature this decade.

According to a review of the latest global data, there have been positive signs that efforts to mobilize finance for nature is progressing:

The assessment comes from an update to the Biodiversity Finance Dashboard , a tool developed by the Department for Environment Food and Rural Affairs for the United Kingdom and The Nature Conservancy. The Dashboard tracks current trends in international biodiversity financial flows and highlights both public and private actions driving the mobilization of nature finance.

The Dashboard leverages the latest and best available data on progress against the finance targets of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF) and aims to draw attention to the urgent need to mobilize increased finance for nature from all sources and close the $700 billion annual biodiversity finance gap.

The trends outlined in the Dashboard show growing recognition of the need to integrate biodiversity considerations into public and private finance strategies. It highlights positive momentum towards adopting innovative tools and policies to finance nature’s conservation and restoration, such as corporate disclosures and positive incentives for nature.

However, more must be done to get money to the countries that need it most. The UN reports that around 60% of low-income nations—many of whom are the most vulnerable to climate change—are at risk of or already in debt distress, limiting their ability to protect their biodiversity and overcome climate threats. At COP16 this year, the world must agree on innovative mechanisms to create equitable change at scale.
The current level of biodiversity finance and current institutional mechanisms for valuing and investing in biodiversity are not at the scale needed.

Governments play a pivotal role in this journey. By implementing measures that mainstream biodiversity finance, and which incentivize positive outcomes for nature, they can ensure that all sectors contribute to the solution rather than the problem.

The Biodiversity Finance Dashboard offers a broad look at the state of global biodiversity finance, using the best available sources of publicly accessible data to provide an overview of current trends. This overview is a crucial step towards expanding our financial solutions to make a truly global investment in nature.

At COP16, TNC is advocating for more countries to outline their plans to value nature, including mainstreaming biodiversity into all government policymaking and budgeting, and developing ambitious National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs) that map out their path to a nature positive future.

Maintaining positive trends towards the finance targets of the GBF will help ensure that financial resources are directed where they are needed most, protecting our planet’s biodiversity and securing a sustainable future for all.

Value Nature Fund, developed jointly by Fondaction Asset Management and Triodos Investment Management, provides a concrete example: a natural capital investment strategy designed to unlock institutional capital for the restoration of farms, forests, and the ecosystems they depend on. For every dollar invested in protecting nature, US$30 is spent on activities that degrade it, according to UNEP's State of Finance for Nature 2026 report. Yet, restoring natural capital can strengthen the long-term resilience and productive capacity of farms and forests by improving the health of the ecosystems they depend on. Closing this gap requires moving beyond commitments and scaling nature-positive investment solutions. Value Nature Fund offers a concrete response by mobilising institutional capital toward the restoration of farms and forests while generating long-term value for investors, biodiversity, climate and communities. Value Nature Fund is targeting € 300 million (US$ 337 million) and intends to invest in farms and forests across Europe and North America, transitioning them toward regenerative and resilient practices. Sustainable agriculture and forestry investment opportunities remain fragmented, limiting institutional investors' ability to deploy capital at scale. Value Nature Fund seeks to address this gap by building a diversified natural capital investment strategy backed by real assets. The Fund brings together the complementary expertise of Fondaction Asset Management and Triodos Investment Management to demonstrate that investing in the restoration of natural capital can support biodiversity and climate objectives while creating long-term value for investors. "The challenge is no longer simply to recognize the value of nature. We need to create financial solutions that allow capital to actively contribute to its restoration. Together with Triodos, we are turning our shared conviction into action, bringing complementary expertise from both sides of the Atlantic to help make natural capital accessible at institutional scale." Stéphan Morency, President and Chief Executive Officer of Fondaction "The urgency of addressing biodiversity loss and climate change continues to grow. Value Nature Fund demonstrates the power of collaboration: combining our expertise with Fondaction's enables us to mobilise institutional capital to restore farms, forests and the ecosystems our economies depend on. Together, we aim to finance change and change finance by making natural capital investable at scale." Hadewych Kuiper, Managing Director Triodos Investment Management The approach behind Value Nature Fund aligns with the objectives of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework to better integrate biodiversity into financial decision-making and mobilise significantly more resources for nature. "Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity calls for mobilizing financial resources from all sources. As highlighted in the Global Report, significant gaps remain, including private finance. I hope Value Nature Fund will help demonstrate how clarity and confidence in potential financial returns can be achieved, addressing one of the key barriers to unlocking and scaling up investment in nature." Astrid Schomaker, Executive Secretary, Convention on Biological Diversity "Public resources remain essential, but they cannot meet the financing needs of biodiversity protection and restoration on their own. We need to expand the role of private investment, integrate nature-related risks and opportunities into financial decision-making, and develop credible mechanisms that support measurable and lasting outcomes. I congratulate Fondaction and Triodos for making Value Nature Fund a concrete example of alignment between finance and biodiversity action." The fund seeks to generate financial returns while restoring ecosystems, strengthening biodiversity and building long-term resilience. The strategy brings together the complementary expertise of Canadian impact-driven asset manager Fondaction Asset Management and Dutch impact investor Triodos Investment Management . For more information, please visit valuenaturefund.com . Fondaction Asset Management (FAM) is an impact-driven manager that creates and delivers innovative, high-performance financial solutions to solve major environmental and social issues, generating competitive returns. extraction.body: Ford has introduced a new Privacy Promise, publicly committing to protect customer vehicle data and give owners greater control over the information they share. The initiative comes as connected vehicles collect more personal information, including driving behavior, vehicle diagnostics, and location data.Announced on November 2, the initiative includes a new website that explains Ford's data collection practices and shows customers how to manage their privacy settings through their vehicles or the Ford App..Ford Aims to Build Trust Around Connected Car Data.The automaker said the Privacy Promise is designed to make its data practices easier to understand. Customers can learn what information Ford collects, how it is used, and how they can opt in or out of data sharing.Kristin Jones, Ford's Chief Privacy Officer, said the company wants to communicate its data practices more clearly and help customers understand their privacy choices.The announcement comes as automakers introduce increasingly connected vehicles with features such as remote start, navigation, and driver-assistance technology. A survey cited in the report found that only 14% of US consumers fully understand what data their vehicles collect.Also Read: Ford Fathom vs Slate Truck: Price, Range, Features, Key Differences.Survey Finds Data Privacy is a Major Consumer Concern.Ford surveyed 1,000 consumers to understand their views on vehicle data and privacy. According to Jones, 91% of respondents said data privacy was an important consideration.The survey also found that customers value the benefits of connected technology but want greater control over their information. Respondents identified the ability to adjust privacy settings whenever required as an important factor.Jones said the company wanted to build trust by ensuring customers have access to clear information about their data choices. She also noted that automakers were viewed as more trusted custodians of privacy than several other large organizations handling personal information..Turning Off Data Sharing Could Affect Connected Features.Ford said customers can manage their data-sharing preferences through their vehicle's center display. sources.title: Ford Introduces the Ford Privacy Promise to Protect Customer Data - DBusiness Magazine
passages: Ford Motor Co. in Dearborn is launching the Ford Privacy Promise to make an “explicit commitment to customers that their vehicle data is safe” and they’re in control of what they share.
As Ford created the Privacy Promise, it surveyed more than 1,000 U.S. consumers — both Ford and non-Ford owners.
It learned that while privacy is important to them, customers understand the value of data sharing.

“Even for a tech-savvy consumer, it can be hard to understand the relationship between your vehicle, the data it generates, and your privacy and rights,” says Kristin Jones, chief privacy officer and deputy general counsel for data and privacy at Ford.
“With our connected vehicle and app user communities growing every day, Ford takes its responsibility in safeguarding customer data seriously.”
Ford says it designs and builds its products with privacy in mind — from collection of data to its use, storage, and disposal.
This can include privacy-enhancing technologies like anonymizing or aggregating data to further protect a customer’s privacy.
As a result, Ford offers vehicle privacy settings that allow customers to control what data they want to share, subject to the features and services they wish to enjoy.
Ford stresses that it never sells data about how customers drive their vehicle to data brokers.

coreStoryFacts.text: Ford has introduced a new Privacy Promise, publicly committing to protect customer vehicle data and give owners greater control over the information they share.

Jones reiterated that Ford's objective is to offer products and services that provide value to customers, not to monetize their personal information..Privacy Resources to Expand Beyond US.Ford said the Privacy Promise website will provide information about its privacy practices and available controls.

She also noted that automakers were viewed as more trusted custodians of privacy than several other large organizations handling personal information..Turning Off Data Sharing Could Affect Connected Features.Ford said customers can manage their data-sharing preferences through their vehicle's center display.

Ford Motor Co. in Dearborn is launching the Ford Privacy Promise to make an “explicit commitment to customers that their vehicle data is safe” and they’re in control of what they share.
As Ford created the Privacy Promise, it surveyed more than 1,000 U.S. consumers — both Ford and non-Ford owners.
It learned that while privacy is important to them, customers understand the value of data sharing.

“Even for a tech-savvy consumer, it can be hard to understand the relationship between your vehicle, the data it generates, and your privacy and rights,” says Kristin Jones, chief privacy officer and deputy general counsel for data and privacy at Ford.
“With our connected vehicle and app user communities growing every day, Ford takes its responsibility in safeguarding customer data seriously.”
Ford says it designs and builds its products with privacy in mind — from collection of data to its use, storage, and disposal.
This can include privacy-enhancing technologies like anonymizing or aggregating data to further protect a customer’s privacy.
As a result, Ford offers vehicle privacy settings that allow customers to control what data they want to share, subject to the features and services they wish to enjoy.
Ford stresses that it never sells data about how customers drive their vehicle to data brokers.
Ford is launching the Privacy Promise to make an explicit commitment to customers that their vehicle data is safe with us and they’re in control of what they share.
Kristin Jones is Ford's Chief Privacy Officer and Deputy General Counsel, Data & Privacy.

Mizzou Athletics announced a partnership with World Wide Technology that will add a new patch to Mizzou basketball uniforms. Mizzou Athletics and Learfield announced Monday that World Wide Technology will be the new jersey patch partner for Mizzou Basketball. As part of the partnership, the St. Louis based companies' acronym, WWT, will be featured on both the women's and men's uniforms. WWT’s logo will also appear on Norm Stewart Court at Mizzou Arena as part of the Tiger’s expanded partnership. "We are proud to welcome World Wide Technology as a partner of Mizzou Athletics and Mizzou Basketball," said Laird Veatch, Mizzou Director of Athletics. "WWT’s founder and chairman David Steward, its co-founder and CEO Jim Kavanaugh and their team have built an extraordinary company with a global reach and deep Missouri roots. When you have the opportunity to partner with a brand of WWT’s caliber, you put them at the top of your draft board. WWT's investment in our basketball programs demonstrates a strong belief in Mizzou and our commitment to competing for championships. We’re excited to continue to build this partnership with an organization that shares our pride in Missouri and our ambition to demand excellence" said Laird Veatch. To report an error or typo, email news@komu.com .

extraction.body: Founded in 1990, World Wide Technology has grown into a global technology solutions provider headquartered in the St. WWT partners with organizations across industries to design, build and scale technology solutions worldwide. The sponsorship builds upon the company’s deep and long-standing connection to its home state university through cybersecurity, AI and digital transformation. Over many years, WWT has partnered with the university on its technology modernization efforts across all University of Missouri System campuses and University of Missouri Health Care. "Missouri is home, and World Wide Technology is blessed and honored to support the institutions and people who make our state special," said Steward, WWT's founder and chairman. "Mizzou Basketball brings people together and represents the competitive spirit, grit and determination that define our state. Supporting Mizzou Basketball is another way we can give back to our home state and encourage the next generation of leaders on and off the court.” “World Wide Technology is an outstanding example of what can be accomplished through vision and teamwork. I have really appreciated my relationship with Mr. Steward over the years and know how much he values giving back to the community,” Mizzou’s Whitten Family Men's Basketball Head Coach Dennis Gates said. “He has continually demonstrated that with his exceptional work with the Steward Family Foundation and with his partnership at Mizzou. Steward’s support and friendship as we continue to build a championship program in Columbia.” "We're so grateful for World Wide Technology's investment in Mizzou and Mr. Steward’s belief in our programs and student-athletes," Mizzou Women’s Basketball coach Kellie Harper said. "Having a Missouri-based technology company with WWT's reputation and history support our team is incredibly exciting, and we're proud to represent this university and our state together." The sponsorship with World Wide Technology was created with Mizzou Athletics in collaboration with Learfield’s Mizzou Sports Properties. “World Wide Technology is a natural fit for this opportunity. As a Missouri-based industry leader with deep ties to Mizzou, WWT shares a commitment to excellence, innovation and elevating the student-athlete experience,” said Josh Pell, General Manager of Mizzou Sports Properties. “We’re proud to work alongside Mizzou Athletics to bring WWT’s brand to the forefront of Mizzou Basketball and create meaningful connections with Tiger fans.” About World Wide TechnologyWorld Wide Technology (WWT) is a global technology solutions provider helping organizations make a new world happen by turning ambition into real-world outcomes. Founded in 1990, WWT brings together strategy, deep technical expertise and world-class technology partnerships to help public- and private-sector organizations design, build and scale intelligent AI, digital, cybersecurity, cloud and infrastructure solutions. Through its Advanced Technology Center (ATC), a collaborative ecosystem featuring state-of-the-art hardware and software, WWT enables clients and partners to conceptualize, test and validate innovative technology and then deploy solutions at scale using its global integration and distribution capabilities. With more than 14,000 team members and over 60 locations worldwide, WWT's culture— grounded in core values and leadership philosophies— has been recognized by Fortune and Great Place to Work® for its commitment to innovation, trust and creating a great place to work for all. Softchoice, a World Wide Technology company, supports commercial and SMB markets in the U.S. and Canada. About LearfieldLearfield is the leading media and technology company powering college athletics. With ties to over 1,200 collegiate institutions and over 12,000 local and national brand partners, Learfield’s presence in college sports and live events delivers influence and maximizes reach to target audiences. With solutions for a 365-day, 24/7 fan experience, Learfield enables schools and brands to connect with fans through licensed merchandise, game ticketing, donor identification for athletic programs, exclusive custom content, innovative marketing initiatives, student-athlete marketing initiatives , and advanced digital platforms. Since 2008, it has served as title sponsor for the acclaimed Learfield Directors’ Cup, supporting athletic departments across all divisions About Mizzou AthleticsMizzou Athletics supports 450 student-athletes across 20 varsity programs while competing at the highest level of intercollegiate athletics in the Southeastern Conference. Guided by its core values — Earn Trust & Respect, Live Our Will to Win, Dare to Demand Excellence and Believe Every Step Matters — Mizzou is committed to developing championship-level programs, creating transformative student-athlete experiences and uniting the state of Missouri through competitive excellence.COLUMBIA, Mo. – Mizzou Athletics and Learfield today announced St. Louis-based World Wide Technology (WWT) as the new jersey patch partner of Mizzou Basketball. This expands upon WWT’s existing innovative relationship with Mizzou as the University’s Official Technology Solutions Partner of Athletics. As part of the partnership , the WWT brand mark will be featured on the uniforms of both men’s and women’s Tiger basketball programs beginning this fall. WWT’s logo will also appear on Norm Stewart Court at Mizzou Arena as part of the university’s expanded partnership with the St. "We are proud to welcome World Wide Technology as a partner of Mizzou Athletics and Mizzou Basketball," said Laird Veatch, Mizzou Director of Athletics. "WWT’s founder and chairman David Steward, its co-founder and CEO Jim Kavanaugh and their team have built an extraordinary company with a global reach and deep Missouri roots. When you have the opportunity to partner with a brand of WWT’s caliber, you put them at the top of your draft board. WWT's investment in our basketball programs demonstrates a strong belief in Mizzou and our commitment to competing for championships. We’re excited to continue to build this partnership with an organization that shares our pride in Missouri and our ambition to demand excellence."
